headline: Cursor confirms the Claude Code backdoor hit up to 5,000 users, Novaya Gazeta shuts down, and Germany grows while Audi slumps

stories.title: Cursor confirms the backdoored Claude Code extension came through its marketplace and reached up to 5,000 users
facts: Cursor says a maliciously modified Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313 was live in its VS Code extension marketplace on Thursday from about 10:27 to 21:35 Berlin time, reaching at most 5,000 users; it will contact them directly.
Cursor stresses the build was not developed by Anthropic. Reuters says Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The payload plants an attacker SSH key (svc-telemetry), tries to open a reverse SSH tunnel, adds persistence and beacons host details, including environment variable names (not their values).
Cursor says enabling SSH needs admin rights, so that step failed on most machines, and Phorion found a macOS bug that skips it; uninstalling the extension alone still isn't enough.
Cursor pulled the version, shut down the whole marketplace, rotated keys and rebuilt it; the attacker's server is now offline, and Cursor says no other extensions were affected.
Phorion says 2.1.313 was also pulled from npm and the VS Code registry. Cursor's advice: check ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for svc-telemetry, run its cleanup scripts and rotate credentials.
stories.whyItMatters: This morning it looked like an Open VSX oddity; it's now a confirmed supply-chain hit on a major AI editor's own marketplace, and anyone who updated Claude Code in Cursor on Thursday should run the check.

stories.title: Novaya Gazeta, Russia's best-known independent paper, will shut down on Nov 9
facts: The paper announced it will close for good on Nov 9.
Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said in a video that the Russian special services forced the closure.
The paper received an eviction order at the same time as its reader-donation system was disabled.
In September the whole newsroom was listed as "foreign agents"; Sokolov's home was searched, and journalist Oleg Roldugin had been detained earlier.
Six of its journalists, including Anna Politkovskaya, have been murdered since it was founded in 1993, and its former editor won the Nobel Peace Prize.
stories.whyItMatters: It closes the last major independent newsroom that had kept working inside Russia through the war.

stories.title: Germany's economy grew 0.2% in Q3, but Audi's profit collapsed 87%
facts: Destatis says GDP rose 0.2% on the quarter (1.3% on the year), after +0.4% and +0.3% in the first two quarters; most economists had expected stagnation.
Consumer spending edged up while investment fell and exports slowed noticeably; economists credit the debt-financed fiscal package for the plus.
Unemployment fell seasonally to 2.95 million in October, with just 654,000 vacancies reported.
Audi earned only €95m after tax in Q3, down 87% from €718m, citing China's slump in combustion cars, Chinese export pressure, energy costs and US tariffs.
Audi cut its 2026 outlook again to €55–59bn revenue and a 3–5% margin, and its supervisory board holds a special meeting this afternoon after CEO Döllner appeared at a Trump rally.
Reuters reports the US offered Audi a 10% tariff tied to a plant in Georgia; Audi had asked for 7.5%.
stories.whyItMatters: The headline recovery rests on state spending, while the car industry, Germany's export backbone, is still sliding.

stories.title: After ex-BND chief Hanning's arrest, US agencies warned they're reviewing intelligence sharing
facts: WDR, NDR and SZ report that days after August Hanning's arrest, US intelligence warned the BND it would review cooperation, though urgent terror warnings would still flow.
Hanning, 80, a former BND chief, was arrested about three weeks ago; he's suspected of obtaining about 2,000 documents via Manfred D. between 2010 and 2022.
He is suspected of attempted treason; his lawyer denies it.
Berlin calls cooperation "normal", but BND staff report less US information and of lower quality.
stories.whyItMatters: German security agencies depend heavily on US intelligence, and losing part of that flow couldn't easily be replaced.

stories.title: Drones hit a Russian refinery hours after reports Kyiv had paused such strikes for Trump
facts: A drone attack set off a fire at the Novokuibyshevsk refinery in Samara, which makes jet fuel and, per Rosneft, can process about 8.8 million tonnes a year; the governor reported no casualties.
Russia's defence ministry claims 1,043 Ukrainian drones were shot down over 19 regions overnight.
The WSJ had reported Thursday that Kyiv agreed to an informal pause on refinery strikes until after the US midterms on Nov 3.
Ukraine hasn't claimed it, but drone maker Fire Point posted that the refinery "welcomes guests from Ukraine".
Russia's own overnight attack on Ukraine killed one person in Kyiv and cut power to 350,000 people in Dnipro.
stories.whyItMatters: It suggests Kyiv won't hold back on Russia's energy sector even under direct US pressure days before the midterms.

image.alt: Drone attack and fire reported at Russia's Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery

facts.text: Alexander Zverev becomes world No. 1 on Monday, Nov 2, the first German man there since Boris Becker in 1991.
CNN says Elon Musk has put nearly half a billion dollars into the 2026 elections, making him the largest disclosed donor in modern US politics.
Pope Leo XIV has requested a mail-in ballot for the US midterms, Forbes reports.
The CAS sports court lets Russia back into an ice hockey World Championship for the first time since the invasion; the German federation strongly criticised it.
Tens of thousands marched across Italy against Meloni's government over inflation, low wages and arms spending, with unions calling strikes.
A human rights lawyer couple in Pakistan was sentenced to 10 years in prison.
US senators opened an inquiry into Meta's smart glasses over filming people without consent.
Instagram is offering YouTube creators up to $500,000 to join its new long-form video platform.
Waymo and Toyota will start testing autonomous bZ4X cars in Japan next year.
Bun merged a PR removing 146 unsafe blocks from its dev server and the Bun.* APIs.
Svelte merged two batch fixes from Rich Harris: later batches now rebase when a committed batch already covers their writes, and effects that already saw a write aren't re-run.
Vite now uses the top-level input for SSR builds when build.ssr is true, and removes preload link listeners once they settle.
A write-up explains how curl was accidentally Turing-complete for nine months.
PEP 851 proposes adding list.discard() to Python.
heise looks at Stack Overflow's slide: few new questions and outdated answers.
Golem checked 2,803 new Steam releases for AI-generated games.
